title: Card erratum / historical override
description: Records that a card behaved or read differently in the past than its modern EDOPro implementation, and how (or whether) the historical behaviour is reproduced. One file per card that ever needs historical consideration. A record with classification 'cosmetic' documents that NO override is needed — absence of a record means 'not yet reviewed', not 'no erratum'. Two record shapes are accepted side by side (docs/research/erratum-state-model-v2.md, frozen for implementation): the v1 shape (`changes[]`, a single linear oldest-to-newest chain, `implementation` for the baseline version) remains valid for every currently-migrated record; the v2 shape (`events{}` — a dict of chronology nodes, each carrying one or more chronology-free `transitions[]` — plus an explicit `ordering` graph and a `states[]` map keyed by event-set) is additive and not yet used by any canonical data file. A v2 record with exactly one event and one transition may instead use the flattened `event`/`coverage` sugar, which desugars to the same two-state shape as a minimal `events{}`/`states[]` record. Which shape a given file uses is determined structurally (each shape's required/forbidden fields are mutually exclusive), never declared explicitly.

strategy.description: none-needed: the modern implementation is period-correct for this version (cosmetic difference, or a documented decision that the difference is not reproduced). reuse-upstream: Project Ignis already ships this historical version (e.g. BabelCDB goat-entries.cdb) — reference it instead of duplicating. custom-script: this project must provide a historical passcode, database row and Lua script. unresolved: known difference, approach not yet decided — formats needing this version fail validation until it is decided or they exclude the record with documentation.

historical_passcode.description: The custom card code of the historical implementation (upstream's code when strategy=reuse-upstream, ours when custom-script).

historical_variant_passcodes.description: Additional artwork-variant codes of the historical implementation (within +/-10 of historical_passcode), when upstream ships several arts.

upstream.description: Where the reused implementation lives, e.g. 'ProjectIgnis/BabelCDB goat-entries.cdb + ProjectIgnis/CardScripts'.

script.description: Path of the Lua script implementing the historical behaviour (upstream path or dist/scripts path).

tested.description: true ONLY once an executable engine-level test demonstrates the historical behaviour — never merely because the script exists.

gap.description: Acknowledges that this version's behaviour is KNOWN to differ from the modern implementation but cannot be reproduced today (strategy: unresolved). An acknowledged gap is a documented, visible divergence: formats whose snapshot needs this version keep the modern card and the validator warns, rather than failing forever. An UNdocumented unresolved version is an error — a gap must be examined, not merely unfinished.

reason.description: Why no implementation exists, concretely (e.g. 'Project Ignis ships no historical version; reproducing it needs a custom script + reserved passcode').

upstream_checked.description: true when the pinned Project Ignis databases/scripts were searched for a usable historical implementation and none matched this version's era.

behavioural_impact.description: What plays differently in affected formats while the gap stands.

coverageModern.description: cards.cdb IS the implementation — nothing else to record. Only ever correct for the all-events (terminal) down-set; the schema cannot know a given `states[]` entry's full event set to enforce that placement (a validator concern), so this branch stays generically available on `authoredCoverage`, but is excluded entirely from `authoredBaselineCoverage` (the flattened sugar's `coverage`), which structurally always describes the non-terminal baseline down-set.

historical_variant_passcodes.description: Additional artwork-variant codes (within +/-10 of historical_passcode), when upstream ships several arts.

upstream.description: Where the reused implementation lives, e.g. 'ProjectIgnis/BabelCDB goat-entries.cdb + ProjectIgnis/CardScripts'.

script.description: Optional: the upstream script's own path, when worth recording.

coverageReuseUpstream.description: An existing Project Ignis historical variant reproduces this state. historical_passcode identifies it; upstream says where it lives — both required, matching this project's own established convention (every reuse-upstream implementation currently in the corpus populates both).

script.description: Path of the Lua script implementing the historical behaviour (this project's own dist/scripts path).

upstream.description: Rarely meaningful here — custom-script means the implementation is OURS, not upstream's; present only if genuinely relevant (e.g. adapted from an upstream starting point).

coverageCustomScript.description: This project provides a historical passcode and Lua script. Both historical_passcode and script are required — this is exactly what distinguishes custom-script from reuse-upstream: the implementation is ours, not upstream's.

coverageNoneNeeded.description: A documented decision that the modern implementation stands in for this state (e.g. a ruling difference not reproduced, or — on the flattened sugar's baseline down-set — the modern card already behaves correctly for the pre-transition era too). No historical-implementation or gap payload.

gap_reason.description: Why no implementation exists, concretely (e.g. 'Project Ignis ships no historical version; reproducing it needs a custom script + reserved passcode').

coverageKnownGap.description: Confirmed missing: known to differ from the modern implementation but not reproduced today. gap_reason + gap_sources required. Forbids historical_passcode/upstream/script — a known gap has, by definition, nothing to reuse or script yet; once one exists, the state's coverage becomes reuse-upstream or custom-script instead.

authoredCoverage.description: The five kinds an author may explicitly write in canonical JSON — v2's closed implementation-coverage sum type (docs/research/erratum-state-model-v2.md §4), one legal payload per kind rather than a shared bag of optional fields. This is narrower than the FULL six-way internal `Coverage` enum the design document specifies: 'unresolved' is real (the sixth kind) but is never authored — it is exclusively the mechanical default for a reachable, non-terminal down-set absent from `states[]`, so it has no branch here at all. Used by `state.coverage`, where any of the five (including 'modern') is structurally legal, since the schema cannot know which `states[]` entry is the all-events one — restricting 'modern' to the terminal state specifically remains a validator concern.

authoredBaselineCoverage.description: authoredCoverage, minus 'modern': the flattened single-event sugar's `coverage` field structurally always describes the {} (baseline, pre-transition) down-set, never the all-events/terminal one (which the sugar never authors at all — its 'modern' coverage is always synthesised). 'modern' is therefore excluded here at the schema level, not deferred to a validator: the baseline down-set is definitionally the card BEFORE its one recorded transition, so it is never correctly 'modern' — if the modern implementation happens to already represent that pre-transition behaviour too, the correct authored kind is 'none-needed', not 'modern'.

eventEffective.description: An event's own chronology evidence — the same shape and semantics as v1's changes[].effective, now scoped to one event rather than one bare transition (transitions no longer carry chronology at all).

date.description: When the NEW (post-event) behaviour took effect in this region, if known. On the effective date itself the new behaviour applies. null while unresearched or when only bounds are known — never invent a day to satisfy the schema.

precision.description: Precision of `date` (default day). A month/year-precise date widens into an interval; snapshots inside it are treated as ambiguous, exactly like release-event precision.

status.description: verified: corroborated by a period/primary source, or by two independent reliable sources — and the corroboration must be RECORDED in `corroboration` below, so the claim can be checked. reported: single secondary source.

corroboration.description: Independent evidence supporting this chronology beyond the source that produced it. Required for status 'verified'.

archived.description: true when the URL is a web-archive capture of a period document.

old_attested_through.description: Bounded chronology: the latest date the OLD behaviour is positively attested in force. Used when no effective date is known.

new_attested_from.description: Bounded chronology: the earliest date the NEW behaviour is positively attested in force.

basis.description: What event the chronology is anchored to, e.g. 'TCG release of the first printing with the new text (DPRP, 2016-09-16)', or, for a null date, 'Konami policy revision, exact date unresolved'.

transition.description: One behavioural question an event answers. Chronology-free — an event's own `effective` block is the only chronology; a transition never carries a date. axis is optional, non-computational, semantic-labelling metadata only (docs/research/erratum-state-model-v2.md §1): it names which behavioural question this transition answers, decoupled from ordering, co-occurrence, and the bundled/mechanically-distinct research classification, none of which axis encodes.

kind.description: What kind of transition this is. Only functional and ruling transitions make a card-implementation difference; cosmetic and engine transitions never substitute a historical passcode.

axis.description: Optional semantic label for the behavioural question this transition answers (e.g. 'search-reveal-procedure'). Documentation only — never read by the selection algorithm, the validator, or any ordering/co-occurrence computation.

historical_text.description: Card text before this transition, transcribed from a cited source. null while not yet transcribed — never paraphrase from memory.

modern_text.description: Card text after this transition, transcribed from a cited source.

summary.description: Plain-language description of the behavioural difference (or the wording change, for cosmetic entries), citing script/database evidence where the difference is behavioural.

event.description: One historical-chronology node. Two or more transitions inside one event is a first-class, sourced co-occurrence claim ('these behaviours changed together, as one historical act') — a strictly stronger claim than the transitions merely sharing a subject; do not merge transitions into one event for thematic/'bundled' reasons alone (docs/research/erratum-state-model-v2.md §5 item 5). A 2+-transition event's co-occurrence is itself a chronology fact needing its own evidence (frozen validator invariant 10): `cooccurrence_sources` is required whenever `transitions` has 2 or more entries, and supports the SAME-EVENT assertion specifically — that these transitions happened together, as one act — never inferred from the individual transitions' own `sources`, which only support each transition's own content.

cooccurrence_sources.description: Required when `transitions` has 2+ entries: evidence for the co-occurrence claim itself, not for the transitions' individual content. Optional and rarely meaningful on a single-transition event, which makes no co-occurrence claim to source; not forced there.

orderingEdge.description: One explicit, evidence-carrying known-before/known-after constraint between two named events. Never inferred from declaration position — an omitted edge means no constraint, not 'chained to the previous entry' (docs/research/erratum-state-model-v2.md §2). before/after key into this record's own `events{}`; referential integrity and cycle detection are validator concerns, not schema concerns. A top-level record `sources` list plus free prose is never sufficient to identify which source establishes which ordering claim — a directly-sourced edge cites its own `sources` here.

before.description: Id of the event this edge asserts happened first (a key of this record's `events{}`).

after.description: Id of the event this edge asserts happened second.

basis.description: date-proven: chronology alone proves the order (§5's PROVEN test) — no further justification needed; asserted automatically when `ordering.chains` sugar desugars a provably-ordered pair, or written explicitly in `ordering.edges` when an author has already checked it. directly-sourced: a cited source directly states the relative order, independent of (and not provable from) the two events' own dates — `sources` is required, citing the source(s) that directly state it. researcher-inference: a researcher's judgement call, not a direct citation — the weakest tier, still required to carry an explanatory `note` rather than be silent; `sources` is deliberately NOT required here (decision, not oversight — this tier exists precisely for the case where no direct citation states the order, so forcing a citation would either be padding or would blur it with directly-sourced; a researcher-inference edge MAY still cite `sources` that inform the judgement without directly stating the order). Chronology that CONTRADICTS a declared edge is a hard validator error regardless of basis; chronology that is merely compatible-but-inconclusive requires a non-'date-proven' basis with an explanatory `note`.

note.description: Required whenever basis is not 'date-proven': explains why this edge is believed, so a non-date-proven order is never asserted silently.

sources.description: Required when basis is 'directly-sourced' (the source(s) that directly state the order). Optional, not required, when basis is 'researcher-inference' (see basis's own description for why). Not required (chronology proves it mechanically), but not forbidden, when basis is 'date-proven'.

ordering.description: The only source of event order in a v2 record. `{}` (both fields absent) is the explicit, valid statement that nothing is constrained — present in the schema rather than merely omittable, so a reviewer sees the absence of order was a decision.

items.description: Pure sugar for pairwise before/after edges between consecutive ids, each requiring basis 'date-proven' (§5's PROVEN test) — a chain the test does not prove for every consecutive pair must be expressed as explicit `edges` instead. Repeating an id within one chain is structurally meaningless (uniqueItems). Overlap of ids ACROSS separate chains/edges, and cycle detection across the whole graph, are validator concerns.

state.description: One authored historical state: the down-set of event ids that have occurred, and its implementation coverage. The all-events down-set is exempt from authoring (always 'modern'); any other down-set the ordering/co-occurrence graph can produce but this array does not list defaults to 'unresolved'.

events.description: Ids of this record's own `events{}` that have occurred in this state (a down-set — order carries no meaning, so uniqueItems is the schema-level guarantee that this array is genuinely a SET, never a second textual encoding of the same set via a repeated id; referential integrity and down-set validity are validator concerns).

status.description: imported: mechanically created from an upstream implementation's existence; classification and chronology are unverified, and formats apply the record only via explicit errata_overrides. reviewed: a per-card review has confirmed classification, chronology (or its explicit uncertainty), and implementation mapping; computed applicability applies and ambiguity becomes a hard error.

review.description: Research state of this record. Absent means 'imported'.

classification.description: The DOMINANT kind across changes[] (severity order functional > ruling > engine > cosmetic; the validator enforces agreement). functional: printed/official text change that alters behaviour — needs a historical card implementation. cosmetic: wording/PSCT modernisation only — modern script is period-correct. ruling: official interpretation changed with no behavioural text change — may need script or engine handling. engine: behaviour difference caused by rules-era interactions, handled by rule profiles rather than card overrides.

kind.description: What kind of transition THIS change is. Only functional and ruling changes make a card-implementation difference; cosmetic and engine changes never substitute a historical passcode.

historical_text.description: Card text before the change, transcribed from a cited source. null while not yet transcribed — never paraphrase from memory.

modern_text.description: Card text after the change, transcribed from a cited source.

summary.description: Plain-language description of the behavioural difference (or the wording change, for cosmetic entries), citing script/database evidence where the difference is behavioural.

resulting_implementation.description: Implementation of the version this change CREATED, when that version is itself historical (i.e. this is not the final change) and behaviourally distinct. The record-level implementation covers the baseline (pre-first-change) version; the final change's result is the modern card and must not carry one.

changes.description: Ordered oldest-to-newest. A card errata'd twice has two entries; ruling-policy shifts and rules-era transitions are entries of the corresponding kind. This positional ordering is load-bearing for v1 ONLY — v2 (below) never infers order from position.

implementation.description: Implementation of the BASELINE version (the card as it behaved before the earliest recorded change).

applicable_formats_note.description: Optional prose note. Which formats actually use the historical version is COMPUTED by tooling from each change's effective chronology vs the format snapshot date; it is not hand-listed here.

erratumV2.title: v2: historical-event DAG
erratumV2.description: Not yet used by any canonical data file — the schema accepts this shape ahead of migration (docs/research/erratum-state-model-v2.md, frozen architecture). `implementation` and `changes` are deliberately absent from this shape: the baseline ({} down-set) coverage and every other state's coverage live in `states[]`, and the all-events down-set's 'modern' coverage is never authored. `ordering` is REQUIRED (though `{}` is a valid value) for this multi-event form specifically: these are precisely the records where order deserves conscious review, so the field's presence — even empty — records that a reviewer considered it, rather than merely omitted it. This does not change computational meaning either way: an absent edge never creates an edge, present or not. The single-event sugar (below) needs no such field at all, since it has nothing to order.

classification.description: The DOMINANT kind across every event's transitions (severity order functional > ruling > engine > cosmetic).

events.description: Keyed by event id, never an array — object key order carries no meaning and is never read as evidence of chronology.

states.description: Authored coverage per reachable down-set. Any reachable down-set with no matching entry here defaults to coverage.kind 'unresolved'; the all-events down-set is always 'modern' whether or not an entry is written for it (§4's named exception).

applicable_formats_note.description: Optional prose note. Which formats actually use which state is COMPUTED by tooling from each event's effective chronology and the ordering/co-occurrence graph vs the format snapshot date; it is not hand-listed here.

erratumV2Sugar.title: v2: flattened single-event, single-transition sugar
erratumV2Sugar.description: Sugar for the common case (docs/research/erratum-state-model-v2.md §13): a record with exactly one event and one transition. Desugars to the minimal events{}/states[] shape — `coverage` describes the {} (baseline, nothing-occurred) down-set; the all-events down-set's 'modern' coverage is synthesised, never authored here.

classification.description: Same kind as the single transition's own kind.

event.description: The one event's chronology, flattened together with its one transition's fields for authoring convenience.

coverage.description: Coverage of the {} (baseline) down-set — the card as it behaved before this transition. 'modern' is not a legal kind here (authoredBaselineCoverage excludes it): the all-events down-set's coverage is always 'modern' and is never written on this shape at all; if the modern card already represents this baseline behaviour too, the correct kind is 'none-needed'.
